facts.text: The README says the hovering example publishes the reference on command/trajectory, the position controller reads it with odometry_sensor1/odometry, and the motor speeds go to command/motor_speed.
The Crazyflie command topic constant is documented as "command/roll_pitch_yawrate_thrust" in the RotorS control common header.
The Crazyflie roll/pitch/yaw-rate/thrust node subscribes to the command topic with queue size 1 and to odometry with queue size 1.
The command message type is mav_msgs/RollPitchYawrateThrustCrazyflie.
The joystick interface fills the command's roll, pitch, yaw_rate and thrust fields.
Joy::StopMav sets roll, pitch, yaw_rate and thrust to zero; it is a local joystick method, not a ROS service or action.
The launch file defaults mav_name to crazyflie2.
The joystick launch groups the Crazyflie nodes under the mav_name namespace.
The launch remaps the controller's odometry to odometry_sensor1/odometry.
The generic odometry sensor macro is configured with odometry_topic odometry_sensor1/odometry.
The odometry type used by the Crazyflie controller is nav_msgs/Odometry.
hovering_example calls /gazebo/unpause_physics with a std_srvs/Empty request.
The rqt_rotors HIL plugin names the MAVROS services /mavros/cmd/arming, /mavros/cmd/command and /mavros/set_mode.
The HIL plugin creates ServiceProxy clients for the arming, command and set_mode services.
The HIL plugin's arm button calls the arming service with True.
The joystick launch fixes paused to true and passes it to the gazebo_ros empty_world launch.
The joystick launch starts joy_node and rotors_joy_interface_crazyflie in the mav_name group.
Joy::JoyCallback sets the command fields from the joystick axes and publishes the command on every joystick message.
The bag plugin advertises its recording service with GazeboBagPlugin::RecordingServiceCallback.
RecordingServiceCallback starts or stops bag recording according to req.record.
The octomap plugin advertises a service named world/get_octomap unless the octomapServiceName parameter overrides it.
The octomap service callback builds the octomap and writes it to req.filename when one is given.
The Crazyflie controller returns zero rotor velocities while controller_active_ is false.
SetRollPitchYawrateThrust stores the command and sets controller_active_ to true.
The Crazyflie controller clamps each rotor velocity to the range 0 to MAX_PROPELLERS_ANGULAR_VELOCITY.
The joystick reads max_roll, max_pitch, max_yaw_rate and max_thrust as private parameters with the MAX_ROLL, MAX_PITCH, MAX_YAWRATE and MAX_THRUST defaults.

joy_crazyflie.cpp defines MAX_THRUST as 8162.0 with the comment propeller angular velocities [PWM], MAX_ROLL and MAX_PITCH as 30 degrees in radians and MAX_YAWRATE as 200 degrees per second in radians.
The Crazyflie node's command callback converts each roll/pitch/yaw-rate/thrust message and passes it to SetRollPitchYawrateThrust.
The Crazyflie node computes rotor velocities and publishes them on the actuators topic only from its odometry callback.
For each rotor the motor model stores the commanded rotor speed, capped at its maximum, as its reference.
The Crazyflie basic world selects the ODE physics engine.
The gazebo_ros gzserver wrapper adds libgazebo_ros_api_plugin to the server's plugins unless the arguments already name it.
empty_world.launch starts the Gazebo server as the node named gazebo of package gazebo_ros, with the physics engine argument -e $(arg physics).
empty_world.launch defaults its physics argument to ode.
empty_world.launch defaults its gui argument to true.
When gui is true, empty_world.launch starts the node gazebo_gui of type gzclient.
The API plugin calls ros::init with the node name gazebo when ROS is not initialised yet.
The API plugin creates its node handle in the private namespace ~ and advertises its topics and services there.
The API plugin advertises the service pause_physics with the std_srvs::Empty type on its own callback queue gazebo_queue_.
The API plugin advertises the service get_physics_properties with the gazebo_msgs::GetPhysicsProperties type on gazebo_queue_.
gazeboQueueThread serves gazebo_queue_ in a loop with a 0.001 s wall-clock wait while the node handle is ok.
pausePhysics calls world_->SetPaused(true) and returns true.
unpausePhysics calls world_->SetPaused(false) and returns true.
getPhysicsProperties sets res.pause to world_->IsPaused().
getPhysicsProperties sets success true only when the physics engine type is ode; for any other engine it sets success false and returns false.
The GetPhysicsProperties response field pause is true if the physics engine is paused.
Among the world-update begin hooks that its comment says apply forces and publish sim time on /clock, the API plugin connects publishSimTime.
World::Step advances simulation time and calls Update only when the world is not paused, a step increment is pending or a reset is due; otherwise it adds the step to the pause time.
World::Step holds worldUpdateMutex while it steps the world.
World::SetPaused stores the paused flag under worldUpdateMutex.
World::IsPaused returns the stored paused flag.
World::Update fires the worldUpdateBegin event and then updates every model.
World::Step calls ProcessMessages after the paused or unpaused branch, so pending messages are processed on every step, paused or not.
A WorldControl message with step calls OnStep, and one with multi_step pauses the world and sets the number of steps to run while paused.

determinism.notes: Event-driven canned replies with no physics step, controller or pacing; the placeholder odometry shifts by a small amount proportional to the command only to make it observable

gaps: the fake is an analytic ROS-free transport model, not a recording and not Gazebo; it answers the declared command publication and odometry subscription and runs no Crazyflie dynamics, controller, physics, sensors, world or ROS graph
the command is a fire-and-forget publication; the fake reports only that the transport accepted the message and never that a controller consumed it, that the vehicle moved or that it stopped

the odometry starts from placeholder values and shifts by a small placeholder amount proportional to the command while the world runs; this is an analytic stand-in for the simulator's response, not physics, a controller or simulation time
the stop is the companion gazebo_ros world pause: the fake keeps a paused flag that /gazebo/pause_physics sets and /gazebo/get_physics_properties reports; it runs no Gazebo World::Step

no unpause is offered: the controller node keeps the last roll/pitch/yaw-rate/thrust reference with no timeout (SetRollPitchYawrateThrust, roll_pitch_yawrate_thrust_crazyflie.cpp:223-228) and the motor models their last rotor speed (gazebo_motor_model.cpp:237-239); the clone states no hover thrust and a zero thrust is not a hold, so the package cannot clear the stored command before an unpause; the operator recovers outside MHS (a new reference or a landing by the joystick, then the Gazebo GUI play button or rosservice call gazebo/unpause_physics)

a live world can be unpaused or stepped by the Gazebo GUI that empty_world.launch opens by default, by a WorldControl message, by hovering_example or by any ROS client; MHS does not watch the flag after the e-stop (safety_status re-reads it only on request)
the read-back needs the ODE engine (the clone's worlds and empty_world.launch's default): with another engine get_physics_properties returns false and the e-stop stays unconfirmed with the latch held

the deployment's gazebo_ros and Gazebo must be the pinned 2.5.21 (Kinetic) and 7.16.1 releases the companion citations name (the clone's master is the Kinetic + Gazebo 7 line; its Noetic line is another branch); rosbridge cannot read their versions
the default command/trajectory waypoint path, command/motor_speed, Gazebo pause/unpause, TF, IMU, camera/depth, octomap and every other topic are NOT COVERED
the joystick launch also starts joy_node and rotors_joy_interface_crazyflie, which publish on the same command topic on every joystick message, so a driver publication can be overwritten

the joystick launch starts Gazebo paused until hovering_example unpauses it; while physics is paused (also after the e-stop) the odometry topic is silent and the odometry read fails NOT_READY at the 2 s wire default; the device resource reads no topic, so commands and resets do not wait for it, and each command receipt reports the values it sent
the rqt_rotors HIL plugin arms and mode-switches a MAVROS autopilot through /mavros services; it is a hardware-in-the-loop path outside this package and is not simulated by the fake
the four command inputs are operator_required; site-limits.example.json is an example overlay for the fake gate only

safe_state.description: The Gazebo world is paused and get_physics_properties read pause true back: no world update runs, so the motor models apply no rotor force and odometry is silent; it is the paused flag, not a measured standstill. No unpause is offered: an operator re-commands or lands the vehicle and unpauses outside MHS (Gazebo GUI or rosservice call gazebo/unpause_physics).
